1|# Review 10: English player and inline pictures
2|
3|## Grok Bot review (round 0, before the Muse review)
4|
5|Full diff `origin/main..ui-english` read by hand. All checks pass locally:
6|226 tests, typegen, typecheck, build, check:isolation, hooks, size,
7|check-secrets, gitleaks. No change to public/music, the converter, or the CSP.
8|
9|Correctness and contracts
10|1. Must: now-playing line does not match the required format. Martin's
11|   examples are `Symphony No. 6 – IV · Tchaikovsky · Musopen / CNSO` and
12|   `Ballade No. 1 · Chopin · Frank Lévy / Musopen`. The code prints the raw
13|   manifest title (`Symphony No. 6 "Pathétique" – IV`,
14|   `Ballade No. 1 in G minor, Op. 23`) and drops the platform for Chopin.
15|   Needs a pure display title (drop quoted nicknames, key, and opus or
16|   catalogue suffixes) and a source that adds the platform named in the
17|   attribution (Musopen, Jamendo) when the artist does not already say it.
18|   The full manifest title and credit stay in the tooltip.
19|2. Must: `core/music-history.ts` has no direct unit test (limit, pop on
20|   empty, null push).
21|3. Should: ⏮ is disabled in Chopin mode. It should at least restart the
22|   current piece there, as it does with an empty history.
23|
24|Layout (Martin, t113u)
25|4. Must: the player is a full-width, edge-to-edge bar and the Source link is
26|   clipped at 1440 px. Contain it with margins, aligned with the reader column.
27|5. Must: speaker icon instead of the word "Volume"; Source as a ↗ icon link
28|   (aria-label and title "Source"); the style select shows its label twice
29|   (visible text plus the select), so keep the label as aria-label only.
30|
31|Security: no new endpoints, no raw errors, picture requests send ordinals
32|only through `pickStartN`. English-only UI: grep clean.
33|Housekeeping: `10-impl-aborted-b.jsonl` was a byte copy of `-a`, removed.
34|
35|## Muse review, round 1
36|
37|Read the full `origin/main..ui-english` diff plus the spec, the three fix
38|prompts, and the Grok review above. Ran `npm test`: 27 files, 237 tests,
39|all green. No code edited, no server started.
40|
41|What holds: selection is style-only with no mode, soundtrackId, or mix
42|path; no-immediate-repeat, same-emotion cycling with fallback, history
43|pop with restart-on-empty (including Chopin mode), and the manual hold
44|all have tests that pin the behaviour. The now-playing line renders
45|`display title · composer · source` from `nowPlaying(track)` on every
46|`currentId` change with the full credit in the tooltip. Prefs ignore
47|unknown and obsolete fields, keep a valid style, and fall back to 0.8
48|volume. Picture requests send ordinals and ids only, never text; the
49|popover needs 3 chars inside the scene, hides on outside click, Escape,
50|page or scene change, request start, and while loading. No new
51|endpoints, no secrets, no raw errors to clients. No Spanish UI remains
52|(the only accented words are manifest track metadata in test fixtures,
53|which the converter owns). `public/music`, the converter, and the CSP
54|are untouched; only `public/art` was added, as fix round 2 required.
55|
56|1. (Should) Contracts still promise the deleted hysteresis.
57|   `docs/contracts.md` says a track switches "only when it beats the
58|   current score by `switchMargin`" with a hard cut at `hardCutMargin`
59|   ("1.5 s for hard cuts"). The code deleted `gatedEvaluate`, so
60|   scheduled selects use only the random draw within `randomTolerance`
61|   plus the min-track hold. Rewrite that paragraph to describe the draw.
62|2. (Should) Contracts misstate the player props.
63|   It says `app/player.tsx` takes "the scene title, a skip flag, and
64|   callbacks". The component takes `track`, `replayNonce`, `fadeSec`,
65|   `canPrev`/`canSkip` with handlers, volume, mute, styles, and playlist
66|   props, and no scene title. Update the sentence to match.
67|3. (Nit) `persist` in `app/reader.tsx` takes a `sound` argument nothing
68|   passes; the one caller sends style only. Drop the parameter and read
69|   the refs inside.
70|4. (Nit) `hardCut` is now always false and `switchMargin`,
71|   `hardCutMargin`, `hardCutCrossfadeSec` have no readers. Harmless, but
72|   name them as kept-for-later or remove them.
73|5. (Nit) The reader parses localStorage three times on mount: twice in
74|   the volume and mute initializers and once when the manifest lands.
75|   Read once into a single initial value.
76|6. (Nit) Double-clicking "Picture scene" while loading starts a second
77|   poll loop of up to 2 minutes; `request` has no loading guard. Ignore
78|   the click while `card.phase` is loading.
79|
80|Verdict: changes needed
81|
82|## Muse review, round 2
83|
84|Checked commits `f24b9cf..HEAD` against the six round 1 findings. No code
85|edited, no server started. `npm test`: 27 files, 237 tests, all green.
86|
87|1. (Should) Contracts promised the deleted hysteresis — Resolved by
88|   `2e086f4`: the scheduler paragraph now describes the random draw within
89|   `randomTolerance` plus the min-track hold, with no `switchMargin`.
90|2. (Should) Contracts misstated the player props — Resolved by `2e086f4`:
91|   the player paragraph lists `track`, `replayNonce`, fade, `canPrev` /
92|   `canSkip`, volume / mute, styles, end-of-track, and playlist props,
93|   matching `app/player.tsx`.
94|3. (Nit) `persist` took an unused `sound` argument — Resolved by `f0c3e76`:
95|   the parameter is gone and the handler reads the volume / mute refs.
96|4. (Nit) Always-false `hardCut` and unread margins — Resolved by `8e39c0d`:
97|   `hardCut`, `switchMargin`, `hardCutMargin`, and
98|   `hardCutCrossfadeSec` are removed; grep finds no remaining readers.
99|5. (Nit) Reader parsed localStorage three times on mount — Resolved by
100|   `f0c3e76`: prefs load once into `initialPrefs` and the manifest effect
101|   reuses it.
102|6. (Nit) Double-clicking picture buttons while loading started a second
103|   poll — Resolved by `1c1aeb5`: both `illustrateScene` and
104|   `illustratePassage` return while `card.phase` is loading.
105|
106|New Must findings: none. The `hardCut` removal touches every
107|`ScheduleDecision` constructor and its test assertions; nothing still
108|reads the old field, and the suite passes unchanged at 237 tests.
109|
110|Verdict: clean
111|
112|## Grok Bot review, round 2 (after Muse round 2)
113|
114|Checked the production build in a real browser at 1280x800.
115|- Fit: walked all 287 sub-pages; none scrolls (was 32 of 223 before the line
116|  budget). Mouse navigation leaves no focus box; keyboard keeps a ring.
117|- Volume survives reload. Fixed in round 1: no hydration warnings.
118|1. Must: mute does not survive a reload in the UI. With
119|   `{"volume":0.3,"muted":true}` stored, the reloaded speaker button still
120|   reads "Mute" (aria-pressed false). The server renders the default
121|   (`muted=false`) and the client `useState(loadMusicPrefs)` initializer
122|   differs, so hydration leaves the server attributes in place. Initial
123|   state must equal the server render (defaults), then apply stored prefs in
124|   a mount effect.

# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

Loading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you
are still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design
question the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository
unmodified, tests included.

## Scale to the task

Skip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves
program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version
pin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or
page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this
session, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check
of the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in
the report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a
specification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.

Any other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: one
focused failing test, the fix, that test passing, and, when a broad run is
required, one broad run after the final edit. A report that something already
built behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.

Before a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one
line what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;
never poll a long run silently.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

Do not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository
has no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when
durable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest
honest verification instead.

On a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains
green and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,
not merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.

## Prove the maintained check

Observe the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe
and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.

Do not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,
or explain why the test's expectation is wrong before changing that
expectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.

Run a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or
proportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather
than after each intermediate edit. A focused regression test comes first; broad
proof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.

Before deciding what a repository gate requires, read what the repository
declares it runs: its CI workflow, its test entry points, and its root-level
scripts listed with hidden entries included. A suite the project itself runs
over this change is a gate, not an optional extra, and a suite that skips
itself when its data is absent is not a green result.

A runner is unavailable only after you tried to make it available. When the
repository ships the command that fetches or builds the missing fixture,
corpus, or toolchain, run that command once and then run the gate. Report the
gate unavailable only when that attempt itself failed, and say what failed.

If the real runner is unavailable but the focused test can still be authored
honestly, leave the focused test in the repository and say it was not run. Do
not fabricate a passing result.

</skill-body>
</read-skill-result>

In [app/reader.tsx](/workspace/wt-09/app/reader.tsx): volume/muted now initialize to `DEFAULT_VOLUME`/`false` so the first render matches the server, then one mount effect parses `localStorage` once and applies volume, muted, and style (style reaches the manifest effect through `prefsRef`). Saves still happen only in the user-action handlers, so the defaults never overwrite stored prefs. Only that file changed; `public/music`, audio, converter, and CSP untouched.
